mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) reduces discount rates for equity cash flows and lowers borrowing costs for corporations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate increase above 6.0% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicate housing sector contraction, which precedes broader consumer demand weakness and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO below 105.0) indicates manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate output and profits, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during industrial contraction regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.0, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal in industrial contraction regimes is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS above 150,000 monthly additions) supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.5% year-over-year) triggers Federal Reserve monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and compressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% year-over-year, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI (CPIAUCSL) for two consecutive months indicate active monetary tightening amid persistent inflation, compressing equity valuations and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL increases for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized) during economic expansion regimes accelerates corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC for the GDPC1 signal in expansionary regimes is below 0.03.
